fields.meta_description: Build audience survey questions for ticket buyers, readers, viewers, and visitors, and save every answer in a database you own.
fields.h1: Build Audience Survey Questions and Learn Who Shows Up
fields.hero_description: Build audience survey questions that ask who your readers, viewers, or visitors are, with every answer saved to your own database.
fields.features_heading: What Comes With Each Audience Survey
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the survey and the database behind it from one prompt, and changes either one when you ask.
fields.feature_1:
Questions shaped by the decision you face

Describe your audience and the one decision the survey should settle. Emergent writes questions that fit both, and another prompt rewords a question or swaps its answer choices.
fields.feature_2:
Every answer saved as a row you own

Each answer becomes a row in a database you own, tagged with the show or issue you ask it to record. Next season's answers land in the same table, ready to compare with this one.
fields.feature_3:
One question at a time on a phone

People who scan a QR code in a lobby or tap a link under a video get one question per screen, with large answer buttons. Nobody pinches and scrolls through a long page.
fields.feature_4:
A results page that splits by group

Emergent builds a results page with the survey: a count for each answer, plus a filter for one group, such as visitors who came with children. Ask for charts by prompt.
fields.feature_5:
Opted-in fans sent to your email tool

When someone ticks the box for updates, the app sends the address and answers to your email tool or CRM through its API. A theater can then write to musical fans alone.
fields.feature_6:
A short link on a domain you own

Custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits, so the link on a lobby sign stays short. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep it.
fields.why_description: Emergent puts no response caps on an audience survey, so a sold-out run keeps adding answers to the same table.

fields.tab_content_1:
The poster budget goes to email

Brackett Playhouse asks every ticket buyer how they heard about the show, in a link inside the confirmation email. Of 1,180 answers across the fall season, 532 named the email list, 371 a friend, and 198 social media. Posters brought in 79. The spring poster budget goes to extra email sends instead.
fields.tab_content_2:
A school board reporter, picked by 884 readers

Each January, the Tarnbrook Gazette asks readers which local topic deserves more coverage. School board meetings drew 884 of 2,460 picks, ahead of housing at 702, restaurants at 516, and high school sports at 358. The editor now sends a reporter to every school board meeting.
fields.tab_content_3:
A basics video every Sunday for 1,710 new cooks

Low Flame Kitchen puts a survey link under its videos asking viewers how they would describe their cooking. Of 3,050 answers, 1,710 picked still learning, 1,040 comfortable, and 300 cook for a living. The channel kept its weeknight recipes and added a Sunday video on a basic skill, starting with knife work.
fields.tab_content_4:
Family tours move to Saturday, when 448 of 640 visit

A QR code at the Sparrowhill Science Center exit asks visitors who came with them and which day they visited. Of 1,020 answers, 640 came with children under 12. Filtered to those 640, the results page shows 448 Saturday visits. The center moved its family tours from Wednesday to Saturday morning.

fields.howto_title: How to Write Audience Survey Questions
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to write audience survey questions people finish, then build the survey with Emergent and act on what it shows.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Finish one sentence before you draft anything: the answers will decide where the promotion money goes, or which night gets the extra show. Give Emergent that sentence in your prompt, and cut every question that cannot move the decision.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Open with questions about what people have done: how they heard about you, how often they come, what they last watched. These are concrete and quick to answer, and they lead into the opinion questions that follow.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write answer choices that fit everyone, then add Other with a short text box for the rest. A visitor who cannot find their answer quits or picks one at random, and both leave a gap in the count you meant to act on.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Split any question that joins two ideas with and. Asking whether a show was well acted and fairly priced leaves you guessing which half a low score meant. Two short questions take a few seconds longer and give two clean numbers.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Ask about age range, zip code, or who came along at the end, and mark those questions optional. Offer ranges instead of exact figures and include Prefer not to say. A question that feels personal should never be the reason someone stops.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send the survey to five people from your audience, not the people who wrote it, and watch them answer on their phones. Rewrite any question they read twice or ask about with a follow-up prompt before the real link goes out.
fields.howto_step_7_des: When the results are in, say what you changed because of them: in the next email, under the next video, or on a lobby sign. People who see their answers used have a reason to answer the next survey you send.

faq_plan.a: Audience survey questions are the questions an organization asks the people who read, watch, attend, or listen to its work. They ask who those people are, how they found you, and what they want more of. The answers then steer a decision such as programming or promotion.

faq_plan.q: How do I create audience survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Start with the decision the answers should settle, then write 8 to 10 questions that feed it. In Emergent's AI survey builder, describe your audience and that decision in a prompt. Emergent drafts the questions and builds the survey, and the answers land in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How many audience survey questions should I ask?
faq_plan.a: Aim for 10 or fewer. Each question past the first few should feed the decision you named, and any that does not should go. Every added screen is one more place for someone to close the survey before the end.

faq_plan.q: Can one of my audience survey questions be lighthearted?
faq_plan.a: Yes. One light question near the start, such as a favorite intermission snack, makes the rest feel less like paperwork. Keep it to one, and borrow ideas from funny survey questions if you need a starting point. Leave its answers out of the results you act on.

faq_plan.q: Should my audience survey questions ask about age?
faq_plan.a: Only if a decision depends on it, such as a sponsor who asks for the age mix or a grant report that needs zip codes. When you do ask, use ranges and make the question optional. If nothing you plan to do depends on age, leave the question out.

faq_plan.q: Where should I post a link to my audience survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Share it where your audience already meets you: the ticket confirmation email, the end of a newsletter, a pinned comment under a video, or a sign by the exit. Send it within a day of the show or visit, while it is fresh. Emergent can host the survey on your own domain, which keeps a printed or spoken link short.

faq_plan.q: Should audience survey questions be multiple choice or open-ended?
faq_plan.a: Use multiple choice for anything you plan to count, and save open-ended questions for one or two spots where you want the reason behind a number. For a quick screen, such as whether someone came this season, borrow the format of a yes no questions survey: one tap per answer.

faq_plan.q: How often should I send audience survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Run a full audience survey once or twice a year, after a season or a big event. Short single-question checks can run more often. Keep each person to a few surveys a year, because asking too often teaches people to ignore the link.

faq_plan.q: Can answers to audience survey questions stay anonymous?
faq_plan.a: They can, if the survey never asks for a name or email and the same public link goes to everyone. Say that at the top of the first screen. Put any request for updates on a separate final screen. With Emergent, the answers are stored in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How do audience survey questions differ from questions for customers?
faq_plan.a: An audience survey asks who people are and which topics or shows they would come back for, and it can reach people who have never paid you, such as readers or viewers. A customer feedback survey asks buyers how a purchase or service went. If you have both groups, keep the two sets of questions separate.

plan.angle: The live SERP mixes question lists (event, poll, generic survey examples) with one survey tool; none shows what an organization learns about its audience or what it changes afterward. This page treats an audience survey as the questions a theater, newsroom, video channel or museum asks the people who show up, and shows four surveys built from a prompt that each end in one decision: where to spend promotion money, which beat to staff, which series to start, which day to run tours. The how-to gives question-writing practice as plain advice, and the FAQ covers length, demographics, question types, tone, sharing, frequency and anonymity with no third-party claims.
